liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Shakedown Street** (2 reviews): Described as one of the ultimate versions of the song; Opened the second set and is called an all-time favorite opener [13][17]
- **Stagger Lee** (1 review): Reviewer had never seen it live before this show and loved the song [18]
- **Minglewood Blues** (1 review): Hammond-flavored backbeat, but Bobby's vocals were unconfident and the performance lacked explosive drive [21]
- **Franklin's Tower** (1 review): Fine and spirited, but lacking a blistering edge [21]
- Singled out as the show's spotlight moment [12]
- A gorgeous version emerging from a freak-out space [13]
- Described as a hot version [22]

## The recordings

- **gd1987-07-06.142087.fob.oade.schoeps.cmc3.mk41.jacobs.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): audience recording; 23 songs; 150 min [1]
- **gd87-07-06.aud.gardner.3829.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 20 songs; 152 min; rated 4.64/5 by 25 [5]. Said about its sound: The recording captures both the music's quality and the crowd's energy [17]
- **gd1987-07-06.148854.senn441.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 20 songs; 150 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [6]
- **gd1987-07-06.senn421.zaleski.gems.84623.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 145 min; rated 5/5 by 5 [8]

## Around the show

- Hot, humid night with a full moon; Jerry jumped up and down; the Nevilles sat in; arena wasn't sold out [13]
- Reviewer was brought by their sister as a birthday present and became a Deadhead afterward [15]
- So humid inside that it was raining; reviewer brought friends new to the Dead, including an older Hendrix fan [16]
- After Samson, the Neville Brothers joined and the music nearly blasted the roof off the arena [17]
- Reviewer drove alone from Rochester NY; early Stranger/Franklin's pairing and the heavy tunes struck them [18]
- The Neville Brothers sat in during the second set; reviewer wonders why it happened only once [22]
- Neville Brothers' two singers, a guitarist and a drummer joined for Iko Iko through Good Lovin' and the encore [1]
- Art Neville played Hammond B3, Aaron Neville cowbell, William Green drums on Day-O and Man Smart [6]
- Reviewer heard this show overshadows most or all of the 1987 stadium shows [21]
- Has rough edges and is less intensely hot than the Branford Marsalis shows at Nassau [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1987-07-06.142087.fob.oade.schoeps.cmc3.mk41.jacobs.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Oade Brothers; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller and Blake Jacobs; source: Source Info: Oade's Master (FOB) Audience PCM; Schoeps CMC3/MK41 mics > Oade M118 > Oade modified Sony PCM-F1; Transfer Info: Master Oade PCM > Sek'd Prodif >… [1]
- **gd87-07-06.aud.gardner.3829.sbeok.shnf**: source: unknown AUD> ?> CDR> EAC> cdwav> shn [5]. Also: Recorded by the Oade Brothers using Schoeps CMC 44 mics, m118, modified Sony PCM-F1, to DAT; Reviewer's first bootleg was a badly worn tape passed along by an older cousin [12][19]
- **gd1987-07-06.148854.senn441.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Ted Mattes; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Ted Mattes' Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 441 mics > Sony D5M [6]
- **gd1987-07-06.senn421.zaleski.gems.84623.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Lucien Zaleski; transferred by Alex Ford and Andy Foust; source: 2 Sennheiser 421s > Sony D5 > Sony D5 > TDK [8]. Also: Master audience cassettes from Mark McCue, transferred by Alex Ford in 2007; Space tape flip patched from SHNID 3829 [8]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Pittsburgh Civic Arena - July 6, 1987](https://www.dead.net/show/july-6-1987) [24]
- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1987-07-06 Grateful Dead Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1987-07-06-grateful-dead-backstage-pass/) [25]
